acronym.description: Short name (e.g. 'MATH-AI'). Empty string if none.

conference.description: Conference id; must exist in data/conferences.yml.

website.description: Official workshop website. Leave unset if unknown — the site shows a "help us add it" prompt.

location.description: Where the workshop takes place, exactly as OpenReview publishes it. Stored raw — the values are free text and inconsistent (six spellings of Pittsburgh, one "Sweeden"), so spellings are folded together for display in lib/workshops.mjs rather than here. Keeping the source value means improving that later is a rebuild, not a data migration. Maintained by the weekly discovery sync; unset when OpenReview has none.

topics.description: Topic ids; each must exist in data/topics.yml.

abstract_deadline.description: Optional. Two-stage venues (~3% of OpenReview workshops) require a mandatory abstract registration BEFORE the paper deadline. Always UTC wall-clock, independent of `timezone`. `submission_deadline` stays the PAPER deadline (the headline and countdown), so the displayed date never rolls forward and mimic an extension; this is shown beside it and remains visible, marked closed, once passed. Auto-filled from the venue's OpenReview `Abstract Registration:` date.

tracks.description: Per-track submission deadlines for multi-track workshops (e.g. Full + Short). The headline deadline is derived as the soonest track still open; a track with no submission_deadline is shown as 'not yet announced'.

openreview_venue_id.description: e.g. 'NeurIPS.cc/2024/Workshop/MATH-AI'. Enables the auto paper list, and its trailing short name identifies the series so editions across years link to each other.

merged_venue_ids.description: Other OpenReview venue ids that are this same workshop — organizers occasionally create a second group. Recorded so discovery skips them instead of re-creating a duplicate entry.

submission_url.description: Optional. Where authors actually submit, when that is NOT OpenReview — a CMT site, a Google Form, an EasyChair track. An `openreview_venue_id` already produces a submission link on its own, so this is for everything else: without it, `submission_portal: cmt` renders as the bare word "CMT" with nothing to click. Set `submission_portal` to match.

added.description: Date this entry was added (used for the 'new workshops' RSS feed).

deadline_history.description: Append-only log of observed submission-deadline values. Newest last. Written by the OpenReview sync; never hand-edited except to remove a false positive.

value.description: Deadline as recorded (wall clock, same form as submission_deadline). null = announced with no date yet.

recorded.description: Date WE observed this value — not when organizers changed it.

timezone.description: Timezone the value was recorded in (e.g. AoE, UTC, or an IANA name). A wall-clock string only fixes an instant together with its zone, so each entry carries its own: re-parsing an old value under a zone the entry has since changed to shifts it by up to 12 hours. Omitted when value is null; when absent on older entries, readers fall back to the entry's current timezone.

submission_deadline.description: An OpenReview deadline value reviewed and deliberately not adopted (typically an earlier move you judged wrong or irrelevant). Compared as an instant, so formatting differences don't matter.

official_list.description: The official accepted-workshop list URL that was checked when a human confirmed this entry is legitimately absent from it — an affinity event, a competition, or a co-located workshop that is not a 'workshop' in that list's sense. Records the list that was reviewed, not a blanket mute: point data/editions.yml at a newer list and every acknowledgement for that conference-year is re-reported at once.

review_ack.description: Optional. Records an OpenReview value that was reviewed and deliberately NOT adopted, so the weekly review stops reporting it. Stores the rejected VALUE rather than a blanket mute: if OpenReview later changes to something different, it is reported again. Set by a human after a review decision.

not_running.description: Optional. Records the OBSERVATION that this edition is not taking place — most often that the conference's official accepted-workshop list does not include it. OpenReview creates a venue group during the PROPOSAL phase, so a rejected proposal keeps a live group with an open Submission invitation and a ticking duedate, which discovery cannot tell from an accepted one. Stored rather than derived because no date implies it. The entry keeps its file, slug, page and recorded deadlines — deleting the file does NOT work, the next weekly crawl re-creates it — but it stops being an Open call, stops feeding deadline alerts, and is skipped by every deadline sync. Set by a human after reading the weekly official-list report; never written by a scheduled job.

reason.description: `not_on_official_list` is what the weekly official-list check reports. `withdrawn` / `cancelled` are for an announcement a human saw. A real event that simply is not a 'workshop' in that list's sense (an affinity event, a competition, a co-located event in its own OpenReview namespace) is NOT this — it is `review_ack.official_list`.

recorded.description: Date WE observed this, never when the organizers decided it — the same semantics as `deadline_history.recorded`.

source.description: Where it was observed: the official accepted-workshop list, or the organizers' own announcement. This is the evidence, so the call can be re-checked without repeating the research.

note.description: One line shown to a reader under the notice on the workshop page.
